title: Latency bifurcation decibel annotated scan — field notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures an ad-hoc experiment exploring a phenomenon we're calling 'latency bifurcation' — an abrupt amplification of tail latency (p95/p99) as concurrency or slot pressure crosses a small threshold. The goal: sketch a diagnostic curve (decibel-like) that highlights where cost per successful query and p99 diverge, to inform fastpath vs safepath routing policies.

Experiment setup (short):
- Cluster: dev-cluster-3 (A100s, v4 driver stack)
- Model: Llama-small-ish replicant (72B->trimmed archetype), two runtime kernels: fastpath-v2 (aggressive op fusion) and safefold-q8 (quantized fallback with conservative scheduling)
- Workload: synthetic sessionized traffic (session length mix: 60% short 1–3 turns, 30% medium 4–10, 10% long >10). Token distribution skewed to 12 tokens per turn typical.
- Concurrency sweep: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64 concurrent sessions sustained for 10 min each step
- Measurement windows: ignore first 90s for warmup; measure p50/p90/p95/p99, throughput (qps), and $ per 10k requests (rough cost calc using reserved GPU-hour rates).
- Notes: KV cache hit-rate enabled (observed 22% global hit in this synthetic mix).

Raw ASCII chart (decibel curve approximation):
Scale: "dB" here is a derived amplification metric: 10*log10(p99_normalized) where p99_normalized = p99_current / p99_baseline(@8 concurrency). Baseline p99(@8)=120ms (fastpath-v2).

Concurrency | fastpath-v2 p99 (ms) | fastpath-dB | safefold-q8 p99 (ms) | safefold-dB | $/10k (fastpath) | $/10k (safefold)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8           | 120                   | 0.0         | 135                   | 0.5         | $18.2           | $16.9
16          | 138                   | 1.8         | 152                   | 2.0         | $18.7           | $17.1
24          | 165                   | 3.4         | 188                   | 3.9         | $19.9           | $18.5
32          | 340                   | 4.5 (note)  | 420                   | 5.4         | $23.6           | $22.7
40          | 780                   | 8.1         | 860                   | 8.4         | $31.4           | $30.9
48          | 1,320                 | 10.4        | 1,440                 | 10.8        | $41.9           | $43.1
64          | 2,100                 | 12.4        | 2,560                 | 13.3        | $68.5           | $81.2

Interpretation / quick takeaways:
- Bifurcation point observed between 24 and 32 concurrent sessions for this mix. fastpath shows earlier and steeper amplification in absolute p99 at 32; safefold appears slightly smoother up to 40 but then also amplifies.
- Cost per 10k requests increases superlinearly after the bifurcation — especially on safefold at higher conc because quantized fallback forced additional p99-elongating preemption in this stack.
- The decibel metric compresses multiplicative changes; between 24->32 concurrency we see a ~2x p99 jump for fastpath (165 -> 340ms) which reads as ~4.5dB on our scale. Useful for dashboards: easier to spot sudden jumps than raw ms.

Micro-observations (from tracer logs):
- At ~32 conc the scheduler began prioritizing throughput over slot tightness; active preemptions rose 3x and context-switch stalls show up at the decode stage.
- Fastpath-v2 shows lower median but higher variance at the moment of overflowing batch slots — likely due to aggressive kernel batching that fails to gracefully degrade.
- KV cache hit amplification: as sessions que back, effective hit rate dropped (from 22% -> 12%) which cascades into more compute per request, exacerbating the bifurcation.

ASCII mini-plot: (decibel vs concurrency, rough)
decibel (dB)
14 |                          *
12 |                        *   *
10 |                      *       *
 8 |                    *           *
 6 |                  *               
 4 |              *                   *  <-- fastpath steep bump at 32
 2 |          *     *
 0 |*  *
    8 16 24 32 40 48 64  (concurrency)

Policy implications (draft ideas):
- Fast reaction: introduce a soft-threshold at concurrency=28 for fastpath routes: if moving to >28, route new sessions to safefold or a lower-priority queue with prewarmed slots. This avoids the sharp p99 cliff.
- Instrumentation: add a decibel-derived alert on p99 amplification (>3dB increase in 2-min window) in addition to absolute p99 thresholds.
- Cost control: couple routing decisions to $/10k run rate — e.g., if $/10k increases >20% in 5m window, start shedding non-critical traffic or degrade quality (truncate context).

Open questions / next experiments:
1) How sensitive is the bifurcation point to session length mix? (run same sweep with 40% long sessions)
2) Can we reproduce on different hardware (V100 vs A100) and with different kernel scheduling knobs? (ticketed: JIRA-OBS-4128)
3) Does increasing KV cache priority prevent the downward spiral by maintaining effective hit-rate during spikes? Quick idea: dedicate a small guaranteed cache slice for high-priority sessions.
4) Should decibel be normalized per-customer (tenant) rather than cluster baseline to catch noisy neighbors?

Notes to self / low-fi TODOs:
- Push a shorter digest for product (one-pager): outline the soft-threshold routing change and propose an A/B with 20% traffic to test.
- Add microbench to perf suite: synthetic sweep with variable cache-hit param to map contours.
- Sync with Rahul re: scheduler knobs; he has a branch for preemption backoff (PR link in linked_artifacts).

References and handy links:
- JIRA-OBS-4123 (owns the monitoring alert workstream)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/879 (fastpath adjustments)
- Confluence sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/decibel-bifurcation-notes

Quick summary (one-liner to share in standup):
Observed a sharp p99 amplification between 24–32 conc that drives $/10k up 30–3x; propose soft-threshold routing off fastpath at ~28 conc and add a decibel-style amplification alert to detect emergent bifurcations early.

-- Ava
